app.title: Food Systems Financing Intelligence — FSFI
app.subtitle: FSFI · Rwanda government dashboard
app.ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources

landing.hero_title_2: Build a more resilient food system.
landing.hero_p1: Food Systems Financing Intelligence helps the Government of Rwanda and its development partners see how to allocate funds across the food system. It supports setting national goals and improving overall food system outcomes.
landing.hero_p2: For Rwanda, FSFI works with 37 indicators grouped in 8 components. Stronger, better-targeted allocation across these areas supports food systems resilience and leaves the country less exposed when shocks arrive.
landing.components_sub: Defined for Rwanda's context and aligned with national priorities.
landing.cta_access_body: Sign in with your government credentials.
landing.feature1_desc: See, year by year, where financing pressure is strongest across Rwanda’s 37 indicators and eight food-system areas—so ministries and partners can prioritize dialogue and keep a saved, defensible record of each review.
landing.feature2_desc: Trace agriculture-related budgets through the same indicator framework—multiyear totals, shifting mixes, and volatility—so economic and sector conversations stay grounded in real programme lines, alongside the stress index.
landing.feature3_desc: Stress-test efficiency, reallocation, and multi-year envelopes—including PSTA-5-aligned views—before you lock in scenarios, MTEF corridors, or partnership commitments.
landing.feature4_desc: Track trends by fiscal year, priority area, and geography where subnational data exist, with reports and alerts that support coordinated follow-up across government and donors.

about_page.hero_lead: Food Systems Financing Intelligence is a decision-support platform that helps Rwanda's government understand where to invest and what impact to expect. Donors and partners can use the same evidence to align support with national food system goals and track results.
about_page.challenge_intro: Food system budgets must cover many priorities. Leaders need clear answers on where money does the most good, how spending links to resilience, and how to explain trade-offs to partners and the public.
about_page.challenge_q1: Where should the next franc go to improve the system as a whole?
about_page.challenge_q2: How do allocations line up with national goals and PSTA 5?
about_page.challenge_q3: What mix of investment reduces vulnerability when shocks hit?
about_page.provides_fsfsi: FSFI computes the Food System Financing Stress Index (FSFSI). It brings together 37 indicators in 8 components to describe stress and pressure in the food system, so budgets and investments can be grounded in data.
about_page.card_assess_body: Shows how Rwanda’s food system is doing across dimensions that matter for outcomes and resilience.
about_page.card_gaps_body: Compares current results to benchmarks so underperforming areas stand out.
about_page.card_invest_body: Supports choices on where extra funding will matter most for national goals.
about_page.card_track_body: Links spending and results to PSTA 5 and year-on-year trends.
about_page.components_intro: For Rwanda, FSFI has identified 37 indicators within 8 components. They reflect the country's context and national priorities. Improving them through clearer, optimal allocation sets Rwanda on a path toward food systems resilience and a system less prone to collapse after shocks.
about_page.gov_title: How government and partners use FSFI
about_page.gov_budget_body: MINAGRI, MINECOFIN, and partners use FSFSI and related tools to highlight priority areas and justify allocation choices with evidence.
about_page.gov_perf_body: Check whether investments are delivering intended outcomes and compare results to PSTA 5 targets.
about_page.gov_adv_body: Share quantitative evidence with development partners so external finance lines up with national food system goals.
about_page.partners_intro: FSFI was developed with leading African and international research institutions.
about_page.cta_body: Sign in with your government credentials to access the dashboard.

security_settings.page_subtitle: Protect your FSFI access with two-factor authentication and a strong password.
security_settings.lead: Password changes and two-factor authentication are enforced by the FSFI backend using the audited Rust engine (Argon2id, TOTP, encrypted secrets).
security_settings.mfa_setup_blurb: Use an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, etc.). Your TOTP secret is encrypted on the server.
security_settings.scan_qr: Scan this QR code or enter the secret manually in your app.
security_settings.backup_codes_warning: Store these safely. Each code works once if you lose your phone.
security_settings.confirm_6_digit: Enter the 6-digit code from your app to finish enabling 2FA.
security_settings.disable_blurb: Enter a current 6-digit code from your authenticator to disable 2FA.
security_settings.password_blurb: Change your password if it is expired or you suspect it is compromised.
security_settings.error_generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.

overview.national_fsfi: Rwanda Food System Financing Stress Index (FSFSI)
overview.plan_actual_hint: No actuals recorded yet. Use the Budget Alignment tool in Planning to record actual allocations and track progress against your strategic plan.
overview.fsfsi_scale_hint: Index 0–1.0 · Higher values = greater food system financing stress
overview.critical_components_of: {{critical}} of {{total}} components above the high-stress threshold
overview.chart_explain_blue: Blue — stress from this year’s data only; funding changes show up quickly.
overview.chart_explain_red: Red (dashed) — cumulative stress including damage carried forward; recovery is slower.
overview.chart_explain_gap: The gap between the lines ≈ structural financing pressure that lingers after budgets improve.
overview.trend_subtitle_fsfsi: Overall food system stress index across fiscal years
overview.trend_subtitle_heatmap: Visual overview of stress levels by component and year

assessment_page.page_subtitle: Run and review FSFSI by fiscal year. Engine outputs are saved for audit and comparison across runs.
assessment_page.saved_list_intro: Open a run for full component and indicator detail. Select up to four runs to compare headline metrics side by side.
assessment_page.compare_need_two: Select at least two runs using the checkboxes to compare.
assessment_page.fsfsi_kpi_explainer: The headline figure uses the latest saved assessment for {{fy}}. When two numbers appear, the headline is cumulative stress (financing pressure carried from earlier years where the model applies it). The smaller line is this fiscal year only. A saved run in the list shows that run’s point-in-time FSFSI; it matches the dashboard only when it is the same save, weighting, and scenario as the latest run feeding the summary.
assessment_page.efficiency_hint: Optimal FSFSI ÷ actual FSFSI (this assessment). 1.0 means actual stress equals the modelled optimal mix; lower values mean stress is higher than the optimal benchmark would imply—i.e. room to improve allocation efficiency.
assessment_page.data_vintage: Indicator inputs correspond to {{fy}} in the selector.
assessment_page.detail_vs_dashboard_note: The top KPI card prefers cumulative FSFSI when the backend provides it. This panel highlights this save’s point-in-time FSFSI. If the numbers differ, compare cumulative vs point-in-time and check weighting and scenario below.
assessment_page.gap_legend: Performance gap: ✓ on or at benchmark (gap ≈ 0). Arrow + value = distance from benchmark for this indicator—not a time trend (arrow does not mean “getting worse over years”).
assessment_page.gap_tooltip_off_benchmark: Gap vs benchmark for this indicator; arrow marks magnitude, not a year-on-year trend.

optimization_page.title: Budget optimization
optimization_page.subtitle: Closed-form allocation analysis from the audited Rust engine: compares your mapped sector budgets to a benchmark-optimal mix that minimizes FSFSI for the same total envelope.
optimization_page.method_note: Uses the latest saved assessment for the fiscal year you select (same weighting and scenario as that run). Outputs are indicative rebalancing signals — not appropriation instructions.
optimization_page.fy_selector_hint: Chooses which assessment snapshot drives inputs; only fiscal years with a saved assessment appear.
optimization_page.no_assessment_title: No assessment for this fiscal year
optimization_page.no_assessment_body: Run an FSFSI assessment first. This page will then load optimization automatically for the latest save in that year.
optimization_page.preview_title: What you will see after the engine runs
optimization_page.preview_running_body: The backend is computing efficiency, reallocation, and ROI from your latest saved assessment. This usually takes a few seconds to about a minute depending on server load.
optimization_page.preview_idle_body: Preview of inputs and outputs. Results refresh when you change fiscal year or click re-run.
optimization_page.preview_output_efficiency: Efficiency index, current vs optimal FSFSI, and component-level gaps
optimization_page.preview_output_reallocation: Prioritized reallocation moves under the same budget total
optimization_page.preview_output_roi: ROI-style rankings for marginal stress reduction per billion RWF
optimization_page.time_hint: Typical runtime: a few seconds to about one minute for all three panels (three engine calls).
optimization_page.analyzing_detail: Calling efficiency, reallocation, and ROI endpoints…
optimization_page.results_lead: Engine output for this assessment: point-in-time FSFSI {{current}} could fall toward about {{optimal}} with an optimal mix; modeled financing slack vs that benchmark is about {{waste}}%.
optimization_page.rerun_title: Re-runs the same three optimization calls for the current assessment
optimization_page.card_efficiency_sub: Current mapped allocations vs the model’s optimal shares for the same total budget — identifies where stress reduction is left on the table.
optimization_page.card_reallocation_sub: Prioritized shifts between components while holding the aggregate envelope implied by the assessment.
optimization_page.card_roi_sub: Ranks components by modeled stress reduction per billion RWF reallocated.

planning.title: Strategic Planning
planning.subtitle: Multi-year FSFSI trajectory and MTEF for country-level decision making.
planning.no_assessment_message: Run an FSFI assessment for the selected fiscal year to enable strategic planning and MTEF.
planning.parameters_help: Set target and horizon; both multi-year and 3-year MTEF are generated. Budget growth rate applies to both the trajectory and MTEF.
planning.horizon_start_fy_hint: Maps horizon rows to FY labels (Year 2 = this + 1, etc.). Default is the year after the assessment fiscal year.
planning.alignment_help: Expand a year and enter component budgets in billions RWF. The national total is the sum of those lines. Your percentage split updates as you type. The tool compares your scale to the plan and runs a cumulative FSFSI projection with your mix, using the same stress rules as strategic planning.
planning.alignment_cumulative_note: Enter the budgets you are proposing for each food-system component below. The tool shows how your allocation compares to the optimal plan and projects the national financing stress score you would get with that mix and total.
planning.alignment_mix_help: Amounts add up to your national total. “Your %” is derived from your split (always sums to 100%).
planning.alignment_fsfsi_compare: Cumulative FSFSI after your allocation (this horizon year)
planning.alignment_worse: Higher cumulative stress than the optimal plan for this year. Check your mix and total funding.
planning.alignment_above_target: Above the planned milestone target for this year.
planning.alignment_prior_missing: Missing prior-year plan data; cannot simulate year 2+.
planning.alignment_actual_hint: This year's actual allocation is recorded
planning.alignment_footnote: Simulation uses planning weights/scenario you selected above. It does not re-run a full indicator-level assessment; for official scores, run Assessment after budgets are fixed in the system.
planning.regenerate_plans_hint: Re-run the planner with the current parameters and assessment. Use after you change targets, growth, weighting, or scenario.
planning.workflow_hint: After results appear, use the tabs below the KPI cards to move through trajectory, components, budget alignment, MTEF, and outcomes without scrolling the full page.
planning.tab_mtef_unavailable: MTEF results are not loaded. Generate plans from the same assessment or open a saved plan that matches this run.
planning.save_state_note: Saving stores parameters and the engine’s strategic plan (trajectory and optimal mix). Budget alignment “Save as actual” is separate: it records scenario allocations you typed for tracking and only works when a plan is already saved.
planning.mtef_year3_off_track_title: Year 3 moves off the MTEF path
planning.mtef_year3_off_track_intro: Projected FSFSI is {{projected}}, above the Year 3 policy corridor ({{policy}}) and/or the operational pacing target ({{operational}}). On this index, lower is better — so the modeled 3-year envelope is asking for faster stress reduction than the budget trajectory currently delivers.
planning.mtef_year3_off_track_levers: Levers to try next: increase annual budget growth in parameters, revisit the MTEF 3-year improvement percentage, choose a pacing curve that matches finance capacity, or tighten reallocation toward the highest-stress components before raising the aggregate envelope.
planning.mtef_targets_curve_note: Policy targets follow the linear 3-year fiscal commitment line. Operational targets use the pacing curve you selected ({{curve}}).
planning.fiscal_mtef_row_yoy: Modelled change in the MTEF window versus Year 1: Year 1→2 {{y1y2}}%; Year 1→3 {{y1y3}}%.
planning.component_table_subtitle: Projected cumulative stress by component across the planning horizon. Recovery speed depends on each sector’s dynamics and its share of the envelope.
planning.component_table_sort_hint: Rows are sorted by the largest reduction in cumulative stress first (best recovery at the top), not alphabetically or by budget size.
planning.component_policy_alert_lead: {{names}} — cumulative stress is still projected to rise for these components under the current recommended mix.
planning.component_policy_alert_close: Consider reallocating from stable areas toward sectors under the most persistent stress while keeping the national total realistic.
planning.budget_increase_over_plan: Planned budget increase (by end of plan)
planning.budget_increase_hint: Extra budget over the plan to reach the target. This is not a funding gap.
planning.section_multiyear_desc: Trajectory, budget evolution and outcomes for your chosen planning horizon.
planning.section_mtef_desc: Separate rolling 3-year plan with its own target (improvement %) and budget growth.
planning.trajectory_help: Projected vs year target; green line is final target.
planning.mtef_help: Rolling 3-year plan with target improvement and budget growth.
planning.mtef_diff_note: MTEF is a separate 3-year plan: it uses the improvement % and budget growth rate above. Its Year 3 target is baseline × (1 − improvement %), not the absolute target used in the trajectory chart. Projected FSFSI can be better than that target when budget growth is high.
planning.saved_plans_help: Open a stored plan, set one as active for the National Overview, or start a new draft. Select up to three plans to compare trajectories.
planning.saved_plans_empty: No saved plans for this fiscal year yet. Generate a plan below, then use Save Plan.
planning.viewing_saved: You are viewing a saved plan. Adjust parameters and click Generate plans to explore alternatives, or Start new plan to clear the canvas.
planning.compare_help: Side-by-side parameters and projected FSFSI paths (multi-year trajectory only).
planning.saved_invalid_json: This saved plan could not be loaded (missing data).
planning.saved_open_failed: Could not open the saved plan.
planning.compare_failed: Could not load plans for comparison.
planning.saved_different_assessment: This plan was saved from a different assessment run than the one loaded now. Regenerate assessments if you need numbers aligned with current data.
planning.save_new_title: Save this plan as the official strategic plan
planning.save_new_help: Plan names must be unique for this fiscal year (case-insensitive). Saving a new plan deactivates any previous active plan for the year.
planning.save_update_help: Changes to parameters or weighting regenerate the stored trajectory. Renaming must stay unique for this fiscal year.
planning.delete_confirm: Permanently delete this saved plan? This cannot be undone.

budget_page.title: Budget Analysis
budget_page.subtitle: Track how Rwanda’s agricultural and food-system budget is mapped across components and fiscal years in weighted LCU billions.
budget_page.scope_note: All series come from mapped budget data, not from FSFSI assessment scores.
budget_page.no_data: No mapped budget data yet. Run import_budget_mapping (pipeline Step 1) first.
budget_page.metric_vol_hint: Std. dev. of year-on-year % change in national weighted total
budget_page.metric_hhi_hint: Across food-system components; higher = more concentrated
budget_page.metric_mapping_confidence_hint: Mapped lines as a share of all lines in FY{{year}} (100% minus fallback). Higher is stronger traceability to programmes.
budget_page.chart_national_help: Sum of indicator weighted allocations in billions LCU.
budget_page.chart_spike_note: +{{yoy}}% from FY{{prevYear}} to FY{{year}}. Sharp jumps can reflect real spending growth, programme reclassification, or mapping methodology changes — validate before treating as a pure policy outcome.
budget_page.chart_general_caveat: Totals mix directly mapped and fallback allocations. Read this series together with data confidence and the mapping quality table.
budget_page.chart_share_title: Largest components, share of national total
budget_page.chart_share_help: Percent of national weighted budget by component (top five by latest year).
budget_page.insights_subtitle: Decision-oriented readouts from the composition model — pair with the reference tables for audit detail.
budget_page.drift_help: Change in percentage points of national weighted total.
budget_page.section_reference_intro: Detailed lines for ministry analysts and development partner review.
budget_page.movers_help: Ranks use weighted LCU each year. Level Δ% and CAGR need a positive allocation at the start (and CAGR also at the end); starting from zero makes percent growth undefined, so those cells show an em dash. Share Δ (ppt) is always defined: change in this indicator’s share of the national mapped total.
budget_page.mover_cagr_hint: Geometric growth of this indicator’s weighted total; only when first and last year are both greater than zero.
budget_page.mover_cagr_caveat: Extreme CAGR usually means the first-year allocation was very small; the figure is mathematically correct but misleading as a growth headline—prioritise share change (ppt) and level context.
budget_page.mover_footnote_cagr: * Extreme CAGR and/or near-zero starting allocation — hover the cell for detail.
budget_page.mover_level_hint: Percent change in this indicator’s weighted total vs the first year; only when the first year is greater than zero.
budget_page.mover_share_hint: Change in percentage points of national mapped total (first year vs last year).
budget_page.quality_help: Mapped budget lines versus fallback estimates. More fallback can mean weaker links to programmes.
budget_page.snapshot_help: Detailed indicator table for the end year of the window (same definitions as pipeline).
budget_page.snapshot_auto_hint: Year-end composition loads automatically for the end of the current window.
